title: Essen & Trinken (Food & Drink)
description: Name meals, foods and drinks — including dishes from German-speaking countries — order in a café, give simple recipe instructions, and compare healthy food with fast food.

notes.heading: Meals of the Day — die Mahlzeiten
notes.body:
Germans traditionally eat three main meals:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| das Frühstück | breakfast |
| das Mittagessen | lunch |
| das Abendessen / das Abendbrot | dinner / evening meal |
| die Mahlzeit | the meal |

💡 Worked examples:
- *Zum Frühstück esse ich Brot mit Käse.* — For breakfast I eat bread with cheese.
- *Zum Mittagessen essen wir warm.* — For lunch we eat a hot meal.

📎 Key points:
- **Zum Frühstück / Zum Mittagessen** = "for breakfast / for lunch" (zu + dem = zum).
- In many German-speaking families the hot meal of the day is lunch, and the evening meal is often cold bread, cheese and sausage — this is why dinner is also called **das Abendbrot** (evening bread).

notes.heading: Food Vocabulary — das Essen
notes.body:
Learn each food with its article:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| das Brot / das Brötchen | the bread / the bread roll |
| der Käse | the cheese |
| die Wurst | the sausage |
| das Ei (pl. die Eier) | the egg |
| der Apfel | the apple |
| die Kartoffel | the potato |
| der Reis | the rice |
| das Hähnchen | the chicken |
| der Fisch | the fish |
| der Joghurt | the yoghurt |
| der Nudeln (pl.) | the pasta / noodles (usually *die Nudeln*) |

💡 Worked example: *Ich esse gern Fisch mit Reis.* — I like eating fish with rice.

⚠️ Common mistake: mixing up **das Essen** (the food / the meal) with the verb **essen** (to eat). Same word family, different jobs: *Das Essen ist gut — ich esse gern hier.*

notes.heading: Dishes from German-Speaking Countries
notes.body:
Germany, Austria and Switzerland have famous traditional dishes:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| das Schnitzel | breaded, fried veal or pork cutlet (Wiener Schnitzel is from Vienna) |
| die Brezel | the pretzel — a salty, twisted bread, typical of Bavaria |
| die Bratwurst | the fried/grilled sausage, often in a bread roll |
| der Apfelstrudel | apple strudel — a pastry with apple filling, from Austria |
| das Kartoffelsalat (usually *der Kartoffelsalat*) | potato salad |
| die Spätzle | soft egg noodles from southern Germany and Switzerland |
| das Fondue | melted cheese for dipping bread, a Swiss speciality |

💡 Worked example: *In Österreich isst man oft Schnitzel mit Kartoffelsalat.* — In Austria people often eat schnitzel with potato salad.

📎 Key point: **man isst / man trinkt** = "one eats / one drinks" — handy for saying what people generally do: *In der Schweiz trinkt man gern heiße Schokolade.*

notes.heading: Drinks — die Getränke
notes.body:
| German | English |
|---|---|
| das Wasser | the water |
| der Saft (der Apfelsaft, der Orangensaft) | the juice (apple juice, orange juice) |
| die Milch | the milk |
| die Limonade / die Limo | the lemonade / fizzy drink |
| der Tee | the tea |
| der Kaffee | the coffee |
| die heiße Schokolade | the hot chocolate |
| das Mineralwasser | the sparkling mineral water |

💡 Worked example: *Ich trinke morgens Orangensaft und nachmittags Tee.* — In the morning I drink orange juice and in the afternoon tea.

⚠️ Common mistake: in Germany, if you just ask for *Wasser* in a restaurant, you will often get sparkling water. Ask for **stilles Wasser** if you want still water.

notes.heading: Ordering Food and Drink — Ich hätte gern ...
notes.body:
In a café or restaurant, order politely with **Ich hätte gern ...** (I would like ...):

- *Ich hätte gern eine Brezel und einen Apfelsaft.* — I would like a pretzel and an apple juice.
- *Was möchten Sie?* — What would you like? (the waiter asks)
- *Die Rechnung, bitte!* — The bill, please!
- *Schmeckt es Ihnen?* — Does it taste good to you? — *Ja, es schmeckt sehr gut!*

📎 Key points:
- **Ich hätte gern ...** is politer than **Ich will ...** (I want) — always use it when ordering.
- Watch the accusative: *einen Apfelsaft* (der Saft → den), but *eine Brezel* (feminine — no change).

💡 Mini-dialogue:
- *Guten Tag! Was hätten Sie gern?*
- *Ich hätte gern ein Schnitzel mit Kartoffeln und ein Mineralwasser.*
- *Kommt sofort!* — Coming right away!

notes.heading: Simple Recipe Instructions — the Imperative
notes.body:
Recipes and instructions use the **imperative** — the command form of the verb. For the informal du-form, use the verb stem:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| Schneide die Zwiebel! | Cut the onion! |
| Nimm zwei Eier! | Take two eggs! |
| Mische den Teig! | Mix the dough! |
| Gib Salz dazu! | Add salt! |
| Backe den Kuchen 30 Minuten! | Bake the cake for 30 minutes! |

🔑 How it works: for du-commands, take the du-form of the verb and drop the -st: *du nimmst → Nimm!*, *du schneidest → Schneide!*

💡 Worked example (a mini pancake recipe): *Nimm Mehl, Milch und zwei Eier. Mische alles. Backe die Pfannkuchen in der Pfanne.*

📎 Key point: in the imperative the verb comes FIRST in the sentence — the opposite of a normal statement.

notes.heading: Healthy or Not? — Opinions with gern
notes.body:
Say what you like eating and drinking with **gern**:

- *Ich esse gern Obst.* — I like eating fruit.
- *Ich trinke lieber Wasser als Limonade.* — I prefer drinking water to lemonade.
- *Ich esse nicht gern Fast Food.* — I don't like eating fast food.

Vocabulary for the healthy-living discussion:

| German | English |
|---|---|
| gesund / ungesund | healthy / unhealthy |
| das Obst / das Gemüse | the fruit / the vegetables |
| das Fast Food | fast food |
| die Pommes (pl.) | the chips / fries |
| zu viel Zucker / Fett | too much sugar / fat |

💡 Worked example: *Fast Food schmeckt gut, aber es ist ungesund. Ich esse lieber Gemüse, denn das ist gesund.* — Fast food tastes good, but it is unhealthy. I prefer eating vegetables because that is healthy.

📎 Key point: **gern** = like to; **lieber** = prefer to; **am liebsten** = like most of all: *Am liebsten esse ich Pizza.*

flashcards.example: Zum Frühstück esse ich ein Brötchen. — For breakfast I eat a bread roll.

flashcards.definition: lunch — often the hot meal of the day in Germany
flashcards.example: Das Mittagessen ist um ein Uhr. — Lunch is at one o'clock.

flashcards.definition: dinner / evening meal (often cold bread, cheese and sausage)
flashcards.example: Am Abend essen wir Abendbrot. — In the evening we have a cold supper.

flashcards.definition: breaded, fried cutlet — a famous Austrian and German dish
flashcards.example: Das Schnitzel schmeckt sehr gut. — The schnitzel tastes very good.

flashcards.definition: the pretzel — a salty, twisted bread from Bavaria
flashcards.example: Ich kaufe eine Brezel am Markt. — I buy a pretzel at the market.
Die Bratwurst isst man mit Brot. — You eat the fried sausage with bread.

flashcards.definition: I would like ... — the polite way to order food and drink
flashcards.example: Ich hätte gern einen Apfelsaft. — I would like an apple juice.
Obst ist gesund, Fast Food ist ungesund. — Fruit is healthy, fast food is unhealthy.
Iss mehr Gemüse! — Eat more vegetables!

flashcards.definition: The bill, please! — what you say when you want to pay
flashcards.example: Entschuldigung, die Rechnung, bitte! — Excuse me, the bill, please!

flashcards.definition: Take ... / Cut ... — imperative forms used in recipes
flashcards.example: Nimm zwei Eier und schneide die Zwiebel. — Take two eggs and cut the onion.

flashcards.term: Ich esse gern ... / Ich esse lieber ...
flashcards.definition: I like eating ... / I prefer eating ...
flashcards.example: Ich esse lieber Obst als Schokolade. — I prefer eating fruit to chocolate.

questions.explanation: Das Frühstück is breakfast. Lunch is das Mittagessen and dinner is das Abendessen.
Die Brezel is the pretzel — salty, twisted bread that is typical of Bavaria.

questions.stem: How do you politely say "I would like an apple juice" when ordering?
questions.explanation: Ich hätte gern ... is the polite way to order. Ich will (I want) and imperatives like Gib mir! sound demanding.
Gesund means healthy; its opposite is ungesund (unhealthy). Delicious is lecker.

questions.stem: Choose the correct translation: "For breakfast I eat bread with cheese."
choices: Zum Frühstück esse ich Brot mit Käse.
Zum Abendessen esse ich Brot mit Käse.
Zum Frühstück ich esse Brot mit Käse.
Das Frühstück esse ich Brot mit Käse.
questions.explanation: For breakfast is zum Frühstück, and when it starts the sentence the verb comes second and the subject follows: Zum Frühstück esse ich ...

questions.stem: "Ich esse lieber Gemüse als Pommes." means:
choices: I prefer eating vegetables to chips.
I like chips more than vegetables.
I am eating vegetables and chips now.
questions.explanation: Lieber ... als ... expresses a preference: I prefer vegetables to chips. Gern means like, lieber means prefer.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a correct recipe instruction (imperative)?
questions.explanation: The du-imperative uses the verb stem without -st and puts the verb first: Nimm zwei Eier! Option 1 is a statement and option 2 is a question.

questions.stem: You want to pay in a restaurant. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Die Rechnung, bitte! asks for the bill. Guten Appetit! is said before eating, and the waiter says Kommt sofort! (coming right away).

questions.stem: "In der Schweiz trinkt man gern heiße Schokolade." — What does "man" mean here?
questions.explanation: Man means one / people in general, used to describe what people typically do — here, drinking hot chocolate in Switzerland.

questions.stem: Which drink would you order if you do NOT want sparkling water?
questions.explanation: Stilles Wasser is still (non-sparkling) water. Mineralwasser and Sprudel are sparkling, and Limonade is a fizzy soft drink.

questions.stem: Put this mini recipe in the correct order: (1) Mische alles. (2) Backe die Pfannkuchen in der Pfanne. (3) Nimm Mehl, Milch und zwei Eier.
questions.explanation: You first take the ingredients (Nimm ...), then mix everything (Mische alles), and only then bake the pancakes (Backe ...).

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly orders two items with the accusative?
choices: Ich hätte gern einen Apfelsaft und eine Brezel.
Ich hätte gern ein Apfelsaft und einen Brezel.
Ich hätte gern einen Apfelsaft und ein Brezel.
Ich hätte gern eine Apfelsaft und eine Brezel.
questions.explanation: Der Apfelsaft is masculine, so ein becomes einen in the accusative; die Brezel is feminine and stays eine. Only the first option gets both right.

questions.stem: A friend says: "Fast Food schmeckt gut, aber ich esse lieber Obst und Gemüse, denn das ist gesund." What is the friend's opinion?
choices: Fast food is healthy, so they eat it often.
Fast food tastes good, but they prefer fruit and vegetables because they are healthy.
Fruit and vegetables taste better than fast food.
They never eat fast food because it tastes bad.
questions.explanation: The sentence says fast food tastes good (schmeckt gut), but (aber) the friend prefers (lieber) fruit and vegetables because (denn) they are healthy.

choices: I don't like pizza at all.
Most of all I like eating pizza.
questions.explanation: The ladder is gern (like) → lieber (prefer) → am liebsten (like most of all). Am liebsten marks your number one favourite.

questions.stem: "das Schnitzel" is a traditional dish from:
choices: Austria and Germany — a breaded, fried cutlet
questions.explanation: Das Schnitzel is a breaded, fried cutlet; the Wiener Schnitzel comes from Vienna in Austria. The melted cheese dish is Fondue from Switzerland.
